content:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate and increased latency observed for continuous-batcher on cluster-prod-west (gpu-pool-3). Metric: 5xx rate -> 7% over last 3m, p99 latency -> 13s. Auto-escalation to on-call.

aj: Ack, I'm on it. Pulling up Grafana and k8s events.

maria: I'm looking at the node metrics, I see multiple GPU memory pressure events and a few node flaps (kubelet restarted) in the last 6m. Could be related to the new batching change we rolled yesterday.

sasha: Which change? The continuous-batcher memory cap tweak?

maria: Yeah the tweak that disabled the max-batch-tokens upper bound for some model variants. Looks like some requests are producing very long sequences which let the batch accumulate.

kevin: kube events from nodes: ```
$ kubectl get events -n redwood | tail -n 20
2026-03-15T12:19:04Z Warning OOMKilled pod/continuous-batcher-xyz
2026-03-15T12:19:06Z Normal Killing pod/continuous-batcher-xyz
2026-03-15T12:19:07Z Normal Started container continuous-batcher
2026-03-15T12:20:31Z Warning NodeNotReady node/gpu-node-17 kubelet has restarted
```

kevin: container logs show repeated CUDA failures & memory allocation errors: ```
E tensorflow: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E serving: cuCtxSynchronize() failed: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runner.py", line 412, in generate
    kv_cache.append(tokens)
  File "batcher.py", line 221, in append
    self._buffer += tokens
MemoryError: Unable to allocate 2.1GiB for array
```

aj: That MemoryError inside the batcher confirms unbounded growth. If the process keeps accreting tokens the GPU memory climbs until CUDA calls fail and k8s kills the pod, then node flaps when kubelet restarts containers repeatedly.

maria: Quick mitigation: can we disable continuous-batcher on the prod pool and force stateless single-request execution to drain backpressure?

sasha: Yes. Two options: 1) patch config to set `continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens=4096` and `continuous_batcher.enabled=false` on the gpu-pool-3 config and rollout, or 2) scale down the continuous-batcher deployment to 0 and route traffic to the legacy-batcher pool (higher latency but stable). Which do we want for immediate mitigation?

aj: Go with fastest rollback to reduce 5xx for customers. Option 2 (scale to 0 + traffic split) now. I can run the k8s scale and update routing.

ops-runner: Running commands now: ```
kubectl scale deploy/continuous-batcher -n inference --replicas=0 --selector=pool=gpu-pool-3
# update route: redwood-route set pool=gpu-legacy-pool --selector=continuous=true
```

ops-runner: Done. Traffic split is 95% -> legacy pool, 5% leftover for observability checks.

support-bot: Notifying customer-facing slack and support queue: "Investigating increased latency and errors for inference in US-WEST. Some customers may experience 500s or timeouts; working on mitigation. Will update in 10m."

tara: After traffic shift, dashboards show p99 latency dropping from 13s to ~1.8s and 5xx rate down to 0.8%. Nice.

kevin: Pod crashloop rate for continuous-batcher has stopped since scale down. Node restarts have settled. We should still cordon problematic nodes (gpu-node-17) for deeper investigation.

maria: cordoning node and collecting docker/container logs + dmesg. ```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
ssh gpu-node-17 'journalctl -u kubelet -n 200' > /tmp/kubelet.log
ssh gpu-node-17 'dmesg | tail -n 200' > /tmp/dmesg.log
```

maria: dmesg shows repeated page allocation failures and GPU driver messages: `NVRM: GPU 0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 23, pid 23456, Ch 00000000` and host OOM kill entries. That aligns: GPU memory pressure + host swapping -> instability.

sasha: Root cause hypothesis: continuous-batcher allowed unbounded token accumulation per batch due to a bad change in the max_tokens gating logic. That caused oversized batches, GPU OOMs, and cascaded into node instability.

aj: Agree. Short-term: leave continuous-batcher scaled to 0 for gpu-pool-3 and keep traffic routed to legacy pool until we have a proper patch + can validate a config change. Also add a temporary circuit-breaker to drop requests that exceed a safe token budget.

kevin: I'll create a k8s job to drain remaining pods and annotate the nodes with `redwood/investigating=continuous-batcher` so autoscaler won't bring them back online until we sign off.

ops-runner: Created ticket RNW-INC-2026-314 in incidents with initial timeline and mitigation steps.

support-bot: Customer impact update: Estimated affected customers: subset of heavy-chat customers using model-x-large in US-WEST. Symptoms: 500s, request timeouts, occasional transcript truncation. Initial ETA for stable fallback: immediate (traffic split applied). Customer-facing update sent.

maria: For the patch: revert the change that removed `max_batch_tokens` enforcement and reintroduce a hard cap and per-request token reject path. Also add telemetry to emit `batch_size_tokens` histogram to catch regressions.

sasha: I'll roll a PR with the revert + tests that simulate long-running conversations producing huge tokens. Will tag aj for quick review.

aj: I'll prioritize review. Once PR is merged, we can canary a config change to re-enable continuous-batcher with limits on a small subset of traffic.

kevin: Postmortem note: we should add a cluster-level protective guard to prevent repeated OOM-caused restarts from flapping nodes (e.g., pod restart limits + node quarantining). Also consider a control plane policy to auto-disable continuous-batcher if GPU OOM events surpass threshold in a window.

ops-runner: Timeline so far: 12:18 - alert fired; 12:19 - oncall ack; 12:20 - traffic split to legacy pool; 12:28 - p99 latency returned near normal; 12:36 - continuous-batcher scaled to 0 and nodes cordoned.

maria: Next steps: full RCA, revert + tests, canary re-enable with `max_batch_tokens=4096` and `max_batch_items=64`, add alert for `batch_size_tokens > 4096` and a kill-switch in routing.

aj: Thanks all. I'll own the follow-up and coordinate the RCA doc + customer communications. We'll update RNW-INC-2026-314 with the postmortem and actions. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident RNW-INC-2026-314 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned owners: aj (oncall), sasha (engineer), kevin (sre), maria (investigation). Will create follow-up playbook entry for continuous-batcher safeguards.
